newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: AFRICA TOLD TO REDUCE MILITARY BUDGETS.
newsitem.headline: AFRICA TOLD TO REDUCE MILITARY BUDGETS.

text.p: A Zambian parliamentarian on Wednesday urged African countries to cut down on their military spending and instead use the funds to promote economic growth within the continent.

"This should be the first step so that more resources are allocated to the economic development of each nation," Frederick Mapunda told delegates at a Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) Africa region conference.
Mapunda said cutting down on weaponry expenditure would also help reduce armed civil strife on the continent, home to most of the poorest countries of the world.
He also called for more peaceful methods of intervention in conflicts, other than the use of military force.
"Regional organisations in Africa should try to resolve conflicts within their localities through mediation, conciliation or arbitration, not by armed intervention," Mapunda said.
